Hi,

I'm having aproblem with the summary data part 5 day summary.
For every ID two da tes are exactly the same. See attached file. Example row 2 and 3, 9 and 10, 16 and 17...and many more.  How do I interpret these and what's the reason for the same. I thought each day will be summarised in one row. I'm not using any sleep log.

g.shell.GGIR(#-------------------------------
             # General parameters
             #-------------------------------
             mode=mode, #specify above
             datadir=datadir, #specify above
             outputdir=outputdir, #specify above
             studyname=studyname, #specify above
             f0=f0, #specify above
             f1=f1,#specify above
             overwrite = FALSE, #overwrite previous milestone data
             do.imp=TRUE, #do imputation(recommended)
             idloc=2, #id location (1=file header, 2=filename)
             print.filename=FALSE,
             storefolderstructure = FALSE,
             desiredrtz="Australia/VIC",
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 1 parameters:key function: reading file, auto-calibration, and extracting features
             #-------------------------------
             windowsizes = c(5,900,3600), #Epoch length, non-wear resolution, non-wear detection evaluation window
             do.cal=TRUE, #apply autocalibration (recommended)
             do.enmo = TRUE, #needed for physical activity analysis
             do.anglez=TRUE, #needed for sleep detection
             chunksize=1, #size of data chunks to be read (value=1 is maximum)
             printsummary=TRUE,
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 2 parameters: The summary is calculated from midnight to midnight only
             #-------------------------------
             strategy = 1,
             ndayswindow=7,#only relevant when strategy=3
             hrs.del.start = 0,#only relevant when strategy=2. How many HOURS need to be ignored at the START of the measurement
             hrs.del.end = 0, #only relevant when strategy=2. How many HOURS need to be ignored at the END of the measurement
             maxdur = 10, #how many days of measurement do you maximally expect?
             includedaycrit = 10, #number of minimum valid hours in a day to attempt physical activity analysis
             L5M5window = c(0,24),#same as qwindow (deprecated command)

             relyonsleeplog = FALSE,

             boutdur.in <http://boutdur.in> = c(30),#duration of bouts to be calculated

             timewindow = c("MM"),

             #-----------------------------------
             # Report generation
             #-------------------------------
             do.report=c(2,4,5))

messages.body_plain:
I just had a quick look at the example file you sent.

The data indicates that the accelerometer was not worn for the entire recording. You can see this in the part 2 output or the QC plot in the QC folder.

There seems to be a line in the GGIR that assumes that this scenario never happens. I will fix this, but best fix for the time being is to exclude recording with zero wear time from part 2 (delete the corresponding files from the ms2.out folder).

Best,
Vincent

messages.subject: Warning: GGIR and GENEActiv data
messages.body_plain:
Message to those of you who use GGIR for GENEActiv .bin data:

For reading GENEActiv .bin data GGIR depends on R package GENEAread. GENEAread was recently updated on CRAN and the new release does not seem compatible with the current version of GGIR: GGIR simple doesn't produce output anymore.

This will be fixed in the next release of GGIR.

In the mean time it is best not to upgrade GENEAread when using it in combination with GGIR. If you already upgraded to GENEAread 2.0.9. Remove this and install the previous GENEAread version with:

library(devtools)
devtools::install_github("cran/GENEAread", ref = "2.0.8")
You may need to restart R for this to work.

Best regards,
Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees
Independent consultant

I have attached the day summary file from part 5 too.

messages.subject: issues on part5 MM and WW summary report
messages.subject_clean: issues on part5 MM and WW summary report
messages.body_plain:
Hi

We are trying to use the sleep and physical features from part5 summary report in our data analysis and the geneactiv data were processed by GGIR 2.2.0 recently. As the very begining, we are using part5 WW report, but we found the variable of dur_total_IN could be >> 1440 minutes since the day was defined from waking up to waking up hours. So we switched to use part5MM report in order to have 24 hours/25 hours for a day. However, we found some issues in the part5 summary and need your oponion how to use the part5 file.

(1) As shown in the .html file, part5MM break the sleep window, is this a bug?

In part4,
filename calendar_date sleeponset wakeup sleeponset_ts wakeup_ts
  0004__018385_2014-07-29 11-44-07.bin.RData 7/7/2014 22.94028 29.78611 22:56:25 05:47:10
  0004__018385_2014-07-29 11-44-07.bin.RData 8/7/2014 23.99583 30.23611 23:59:45 06:14:10

In part 5MM,
14 0004__018385_2014-07-29 11-44-07.bin.RData 2014-07-08 23.99583 29.78611 23:59:45 05:47:10

(2) Found missingness of sleeponset in part5MM
(3) In both part5MM and part5WW files, we found some days with sleeponset> wakeup
(4) We found sleepefficiency errors in part5 when we use sleepdurationInSpt/SptDuration from part4.
(4) There are a small portion of mismatch between part4 and part5WW caused by
        a) part5WW lost one hour in the waking time on the day of time change
        b) part5WW made a mistake by not adding 24 hours in wakeup time
        c) Unknown reasons.

We are struggling on how to extract features such as sleeponset, wakeup, N_atleast5minwakenight,sleep_efficiency, dur_total_, L5, L5time for months. Hope to get help from you.

Thank you so much.
Best,
Dora

We have raw accelerometer data collected from previous study where participants don't wear the accelerometer for 24-hr but rather during waking hours only. We are interested in using GGIR to analyze these raw data files. To be able to calculate properly does GGIR need to have continuous 24-hour wear?
Thanks,
Natascja

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Newbie: GGIR analysis - non 24-hr wear
messages.body_plain:
Continuous 24-hour wear is not required for GGIR.

Possibly using relyonguider = TRUE will work better, especially if you would have sleep diary to rely on. Further you may want to lower the inclusion criteria for a valid day (arguments: includedaycrit and includedaycrit.part5).

Best, Vincent
